subject: Transition to annual prepay — exit credit & phased ramp proposal
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@nimbushealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tkeller@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Transitioning billing to annual prepay — questions on exit credits & ramp

Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Nimbus is seriously considering moving from our current month-to-month usage model to a 12–24 month annual prepay to get better unit economics. Before we take that step, procurement and finance have a couple of sticking points we need to understand:

- Underutilization protection: if our usage in the first 6 months is < 50% of committed tokens/month, what kind of credit or bridge do you offer?
- Exit / early-termination credit: if we prepay and then have to exit in year 1, is there a pro-rated refund or credit towards other services?
- Phased payments: can we split the annual prepay into 2 or 3 payments over the first year to smooth cashflow?
- KPIs & check-ins: procurement wants a quarterly cadence with explicit usage KPIs and a remediation path (e.g., step-downs or refund triggers).

Also attaching our internal usage report for Q1–Q3 so you can see expected ramp patterns (nimbus_usage_report_Q1-Q3.csv).

Can you share a concrete proposal that includes ramp milestones, the exact mechanics of any bridge/exit credit, and how billing will appear in the marketplace / PO process?

Best,
Asha Rao
VP of Product
Nimbus Health

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tkeller@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transitioning billing to annual prepay — questions on exit credits & ramp

Asha — great to hear you and the team are ready to evaluate prepay. Quick answers and a proposal sketch below; attaching a cleaner spreadsheet (redacted_prepay_options_v2.xlsx) with numeric examples.

Proposal sketch (12-month example):
- Discount structure: 10% for 12mo annual prepay, 17% for 24mo (applies to model token rates).
- Phased payments: we can split the annual prepay into up to 3 invoices (40% / 30% / 30%) within the first 90 days; Payments must hit agreed milestones to trigger the later invoices.
- Underutilization bridge credit: if actual usage < 60% of committed in months 1–3, Redwood will issue a one-time credit covering up to 30% of the unused committed spend, applied as account credit in month 4. This is intended as a bridge while you ramp.
- Exit mechanics: early termination in year 1 results in a pro-rated unused-commit credit minus a 15% administrative fee; year 2+ prorated refund/credit with 10% fee.
- KPIs & check-ins: quarterly business reviews (QBRs) with usage vs committed KPIs; at the first QBR we will evaluate ramp and, if needed, invoke the bridge.

Open items we should confirm with legal/procurement: acceptable language for the exit credit and precise definitions for "committed usage" and "ramp".

Can we set up a 30‑minute call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet and a short MOU? If that works I’ll loop in Aditya and legal for the redlines.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fw: Transitioning billing to annual prepay — exit credit & phased ramp proposal

Looping you both in with suggested concessions and legal approach. Vanessa — high-level thoughts:

- Make the bridge credit time-boxed and KPI-tethered: cover first 3 months only, triggered if month-average < 60% of committed tokens. Cap the total bridge at 25% of annual committed spend to limit exposure.
- Exit credit: frame as "unused-commit credit" that can only be used against future Redwood invoices for 12 months (no cash refunds unless exceptional). This reduces cash refund risk and encourages continuing usage.
- Phased payments: accept 3-way split but require each tranche to be invoiced within 90 days and linked to a signed MOU; late payment voids the later tranche discount.
- SLA & remediation: include a performance breakpoint — if latency SLO misses occur >2x in a month, customer can request an operational remediation plan; not an automatic termination right.

I drafted some contract language and redlines for the MOU and SOW — attaching legal_redlines_draft.docx. Lauren — can you review the fee/credit caps and confirm these look acceptable from a finance risk perspective?

Aditya
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@nimbushealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tkeller@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transitioning billing to annual prepay — exit credit & phased ramp proposal

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we sign an MOU:

1) Can you convert the bridge credit into a guaranteed minimum usage guarantee for months 1–3 (e.g., Redwood credits us if usage < 60% but the credit is applied automatically at month 4)? The procurement team prefers deterministic triggers rather than discretionary remediation.
2) Marketplace billing: we will buy through our cloud marketplace resale program for procurement tracking — how will that interact with your phased invoices and credits?
3) Contract language: can the unused-commit credit be used to offset 3rd-party consult or integration fees (we sometimes prefer to apply credits to partner services)? Procurement flagged this as important.

Attaching our PO template (procurement_po_template.pdf) — it contains the procurement contact and remittance info the finance team needs.

If we can get an MOU that spells these things out, we can circulate for internal approval next week.

Best,
Asha

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@nimbushealth.com>, Tom Keller <tkeller@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transitioning billing to annual prepay — exit credit & phased ramp proposal

Asha / Tom — thanks for the quick feedback. Per your asks we updated the MOU draft to be explicit:

- Bridge credit is an automatic credit applied at month 4 if average usage across months 1–3 is < 60% of committed tokens; formula and cap are in Section 2.2.
- Unused-commit credit is allowed to offset Redwood invoices and approved third-party services procured via Redwood's marketplace (Section 2.4).
- Marketplace billing flow: Redwood will invoice the first tranche directly to Nimbus; subsequent credits and offsets will be represented on the marketplace reconciliation report and via a monthly credit memo.

I attached the draft MOU (MOU_nimbus-prepay-annual-2026.pdf) and included the numeric example workbook. If this looks good I propose:
- Sign MOU this week
- Invoice tranche 1 upon signature (40%)
- QBR at month 3 to review ramp; bridge credit (if any) applied in month 4

Proposed meeting: 2026-09-06 10:00 AM PT (30 min). I’ll send a calendar invite if that slot works.

Thanks all — excited to get this over the line.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
